_comment: Approved developer tooling baked into the custom UDI.
This file is the single source of truth. The Containerfile reads it at
build time, scripts/check-extensions.sh checks the pins against upstream,
and capabilities-configmap.yaml publishes it to the cluster so a self-service
form can offer exactly what the image actually contains rather than a
Pinned versions, not 'latest'. An image whose contents depend on the day it
was built cannot be reasoned about, and the whole argument for baking tools
in rather than downloading them at workspace start is a supply chain you
can point at. sha256 is verified during the build; a mismatch fails it.
kind: 'vscode-extension' is a .vsix installed by che-code via
DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS. kind: 'binary' is a tarball on PATH, which works in any
editor and in a plain terminal.

tools.description: Agentic coding assistant. Reads, edits and runs commands in the workspace.
notes: Needs an explicit permission block or it silently does nothing - it waits
on an approval that never arrives and then reports success having made no
Sends a ~20.6k token system prompt before the user types anything, so a
small context window makes it unusable rather than merely slow.

tools.description: Thin shim that opens the OpenCode CLI in a terminal.
notes: About 2 KB of JavaScript. It launches the CLI and nothing else, so it is
useless without opencode-cli and pointless outside che-code.

tools.description: Terminal coding agent. The substantive half of OpenCode.
notes: Previously pulled from /releases/latest/download, which made every image
build a different image. Pinned here.
Runs in a terminal, so unlike the extensions it works under any editor.
